outcome: Experiment re-entry now prioritizes the latest numbered revision without losing Working-copy recovery
owner_impact: When you return to an owned Experiment, the Lab opens its newest numbered revision instead of automatically dropping you into an older Working copy. Any Working copy is still preserved at the top of revision history and can be opened explicitly. A new Discard Working copy action lets you remove obsolete human work after confirmation and immediately return to the latest numbered revision.

next.text: The bounded #409 revision re-entry/discard correction is complete. The living #273 UI/UX lane remains evidence-driven, with no automatic successor and no owner action required.

technical_evidence: loadRemoteExperiment preserves any owner Working copy in memory/history but always selects and applies the current numbered Experiment head on re-entry.
Working copy remains explicitly selectable through the existing revision-history entry and its base-revision provenance is unchanged.

Discard Working copy requires confirmation, waits for any pointer-boundary autosave already in flight, deletes only the current owner's experiment_working_copies row, and reloads the newest numbered revision.
The existing owner-only Working-copy delete RLS policy remains authoritative; no database migration or authorization broadening is introduced.
Focused #409 regression tests lock the latest-revision re-entry default, Working-copy recoverability, discard visibility, owner scoping, and latest-revision landing behavior.
No scientific/runtime semantics, connector contract, CI/CD, polling, retry, timeout, scheduling, or project-development workflow rule changed.
